result.rationale: The diff shows `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` — a strict equality comparison with no normalization (toLowerCase). Email casing differences (e.g., stored as John@Example.com, session as john@example.com) would cause a legitimate attendee to be rejected with FORBIDDEN. The mechanism is visible directly in the new code; email case-insensitivity is a well-known real-world requirement. Note the code lowercases blacklisted emails but not this comparison, confirming the inconsistency is real.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a case-sensitivity issue at line 52 in addGuests.handler.ts. The code uses `booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)` which performs a case-sensitive comparison. Email addresses are case-insensitive by RFC standards, so if a user registered with 'User@Example.com' but the booking stored 'user@example.com', the authorization check would fail even though they are the same person. This is a real bug that could deny legitimate attendees the ability to add guests.
